# quectel-em160r-gl

> Quectel EM160R-GL — LTE Cat-16 modem on USB in QMI mode, with a resume step for the SIM that wedges after sleep

**Vendor:** Quectel  ·  **class:** [wwan-modem](wwan-modem-class.md)

Status: **untested** — catalogued from documented sources, not yet proven here.

**Not maintainer-verified**: nobody on this project has run this hardware yet. The two facts are recorded separately on purpose (D-027) — a correct recipe and a tested device are different claims.

## What it is

A Quectel EM160R-GL, an LTE Cat-16 modem in an M.2 slot that presents on the USB bus as 2c7c:0620 and is driven in QMI mode (qmi_wwan, control node /dev/cdc-wdm0). It is parked and woken like any WWAN modem through the wwan-modem class.

## What you can do with it

Carry the station's data link under ModemManager and NetworkManager, and be parked and woken from the CLI, the generated menu entries or the tray. Its SIM wedge after sleep is detected and recovered by the resume step.

## Setup

Install libqmi-utils (qmicli), then run `hammunition hardware apply`, which installs the resume step and says what it writes first. A SIM and an APN are the operator's. Parking and waking have not been run on this card.

## Known problems

After a suspend or a boot the SIM application can come back `illegal` and ModemManager gives up on the modem; the resume step recovers it once per event. If that fails, the manual steps are printed in `journalctl -u hammunition-modem-resume` and in its exit status. Parking has not been run on this card (unmeasured).

## After suspend

`hammunition hardware apply` installs a resume step for this device: `modem_sim_recover`.

Measured on the field laptop (issue #427, 2026-10-26 boot and 2026-10-27 resume): the card comes back with its USIM application in QMI state `illegal` while `AT+CPIN?` says READY and the QMI card state is `present`. ModemManager fails initialization ("Illegal SIM/USIM application state"), marks the modem `failed: sim-missing` and never retries, so NetworkManager shows the card unavailable. A SIM power cycle (`qmicli --uim-sim-power-off=1` then `--uim-sim-power-on=1`) with ModemManager stopped returned the application to `ready`, and after a ModemManager start the modem registered and carried traffic. `hammunition hardware apply` installs hammunition-modem-resume.service, which after every suspend, hibernation and boot reads the card status and only on `illegal` makes ONE such attempt as root (`quectel-usbnet sim-recover` when installed, else qmicli), then starts ModemManager again whatever happened. It exits non-zero and prints the manual steps if the application does not come back `ready`. `hammunition hardware state` shows "SIM wedged" while the wedge stands. It never parks or wakes anything, and does nothing when the modem is parked. The recovery sequence is measured; the unit's run across a real suspend is not yet.

See [after suspend](power-control.md#after-suspend) for what the step installs, how to inspect it and how to reverse it.

## How it identifies itself

| USB id | What | Confirmed | Node |
|---|---|---|---|
| `2c7c:0620` | Quectel EM160R-GL LTE modem, QMI mode (/dev/cdc-wdm0) | yes | serial |

**⚠ `2c7c:0620` is not unique to this device** (shared_across_products; also used by: other Quectel modules and firmware modes under vendor 2c7c). Quectel's 2c7c vendor identifier is shared by its whole module range (the catalog's generated ambiguity list already records 2c7c:0125, the EC25), and the same product number can be presented in different firmware modes (QMI, MBIM, RMNET). Only the device that was read carries it here.
